notes:
Summary: Aperture Systems is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency chat and reranking workload. They run customer-facing assistants that require predictable per-request tail latency and SLA-backed throughput. Strong emphasis on VPC deployment and on-prem option for regulated customers.

Conversation fragments / call notes: 
- "Customer: 'We need p95 under 150ms for typical 64-token responses at 50 qps'" 
- Interested in reserved GPU planning (capacity forecast for seasonal peaks).
- Wants model fallbacks: high-accuracy variant during business hours, cheaper quantized variant for background tasks.
- Concern: network egress + data residency for EU customers.
- Legal requests redlines on retention and audit logging (asked for encryption-at-rest + HSM/KMS).

Internal: AE/Jordan ran vendor readout 2026-02-18; SE Luis completed initial bench runs 2026-02-26 and shared results. CSM Maya looping in for onboarding checklist once POC signed.

Key commitment asked: 30-day POC with throughput guarantees (sustained 50 qps, burst to 200 qps for 10 min), soak test 72h for stability.

Stated constraints: cannot ship customer data to third-country regions for EU accounts, require SSO + audit logs on day 1.

Quoted from call: 'We will push a full-scope soak test — if latency and jitter are within SLOs we sign enterprise contract.'

poc_summary: Objective: Validate Redwood Dedicated can meet p95 latency SLO of 150ms for 64-token average chat replies at sustained 50 qps with vertical scaling to 200 qps burst. Tests: (1) Load test (linear ramp to steady 50 qps, then bursts to 200 qps), (2) Soak test (72 hours at production-like distribution), (3) Stress test (sustained QPS until graceful degradation observed), (4) Accuracy/regression checks vs baseline model. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate, retry rate, error rate. Deliverables: benchmark report, recommended reserved GPU plan (SKU + count), ingress/egress cost estimate, SLA language draft for inclusion in enterprise agreement.
poc_plan:
Plan details:
- Environment: Dedicated VPC deployment in us-east-1 with private control plane.
- Models: primary: open-llm-high-accuracy (fp16 quantized), fallback: open-llm-low-cost (int8).
- Load profile: synthetic driver using customer's 3k prompt corpus; token length distribution mirrored from production (median 48 tokens, 95th 320 tokens).
- Ramp schedule: 0 -> 50 qps over 10 min, hold 6h, then 10x burst to 200 qps (10 min), repeat hourly for 8 hours.
- Soak: 72h with diurnal pattern supplied.
- Observability: per-request tracing, token-level cost breakdown, per-model latency histograms, KVMetrics for cache hit-rate.
- Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 150ms for >=95% of steady-state windows; no more than 0.1% 5xx errors; GPU OOMs = 0.
- Rollout: start with two nodes (N1) for baseline, then scale to N2 per kernel recommendations.
- Contingency: automatic fallback to smaller model if p95 breaches for >10min; SE to notify and toggle routing policy.
po_metrics_from_first_run: baseline run 2026-02-26: sustained 25 qps -> p95 210ms, p99 480ms
cache disabled: GPU utilization 60% at 25 qps; enabling KV cache projected to reduce p95 by ~30%
quantized int8 variant reduced median latency ~20% but increased variance for long-context prompts
commercial_notes: AE proposed a 30-day POC SOW with refundable credit against first reserved term. Customer prefers monthly reserved plan with option to convert to annual. Pricing sensitivity on committed GPUs — asked for 2-tier pricing (business hours high-throughput vs off-peak cheap credits).
legal_and_security:
Legal: redline requested on data residency and retention; security wants SOC2 + encryption-at-rest + KMS/HSM support. SIEM forwarding and audit logging required for first 90 days of POC.
- Action: share Redwood SOC2 report and KMS integration guide; propose data residency by region config in SOW.
